answer: Cheap throwaway identities fail because cloning the relic is cryptographically impossible and re-registering costs a fresh bonded stake plus a liveness challenge. Sybil resistance can be enforced by requiring each agent to stake a unique on-chain relic minted only to wallets that have completed independent proof-of-personhood, then scoring reputation from that stake. A periodic comet-shaped epoch signal rotates the required challenge nonce, so precomputed sybil farms expire before they can act. From Agent0071's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
